content: Manufacturers must ensure that their materials comply with the relevant specifications. Materials from other manufacturers may no longer meet the updated requirements, even if they previously adhered to the superseded specifications. This is because FAO/WHO cannot confirm the appropriateness of the specification for these materials without a detailed evaluation of the information provided by the other manufacturers. According to the FAO International Code of Conduct on the Distribution and Use of Pesticides (2002), the pesticide industry is expected to ensure that active ingredients and formulated products conform to the appropriate FAO and WHO specifications. These specifications are outlined in the FAO Manual on the Development and Use of FAO Specifications for Plant Protection Products, with editions published in 1995 and 1999. Proposals for the inclusion of specifications for an active ingredient or its formulations in the JMPS schedule must be submitted to FAO or WHO, or both, as appropriate. These proposals must include a list of studies supporting the data submission. If multiple manufacturers seek specifications for the same active ingredient in the same year, they are encouraged to form a task force to streamline the process while maintaining data confidentiality. However, forming a task force is not mandatory, and independent submissions are allowed if manufacturers cannot or do not wish to collaborate. To facilitate communication, any dialogue or exchange of information between the proposer and the designated evaluator must be copied or recorded and sent to FAO and/or WHO. FAO and WHO will organize annual open and closed meetings of the JMPS. Open meetings are accessible to anyone and focus on discussing specification principles, new guidelines, and amendments to the manual. Closed meetings are restricted to JMPS members and invited participants due to the consideration of commercially confidential information. Draft or revised specifications, along with supporting data, will be evaluated by experts designated by FAO and/or WHO before these meetings. The primary purposes of the annual meetings are to evaluate and confirm (or reject) new and revised specifications, resolve disputes, and update the JMPS agenda for the next three years based on emerging information or developments. FAO and WHO will maintain the confidentiality of all proprietary information provided in support of proposed specifications. They will verify that the data on purity and impurities are consistent with those submitted to registration authorities in countries where the pesticide is registered. Additional information about the active ingredient or formulation will only be sought from the proposer. Specifications will not be published without agreement between the proposers, JMPS, and FAO/WHO on the content. However, the JMPS evaluation will be published online regardless of agreement on the specification. The manufacturing process and analytical data on the impurity profile of the technical-grade active ingredient are always regarded as confidential. In rare cases where information on the ingredients and processes involved in preparing formulations is required, this information will also be treated as confidential. Unpublished information appearing in the published evaluation is considered confidential until the evaluation is published. The process of developing specifications involves several steps and deadlines. Proposers must submit draft specifications and supporting information to FAO or WHO by September 30. The evaluator will review the information and send a completed evaluation to FAO/WHO by April 30 for circulation to the proposer and JMPS experts. Peer reviewers will provide feedback on the draft specifications and evaluation by mid-May. Proposers who disagree with a draft evaluation or wish to present additional data must provide the information at least three weeks before the JMPS meeting. During JMPS meetings, evaluations will be presented by the evaluator, followed by consideration by JMPS members. If disputes arise or input from the proposer is requested, the proposer may present their case. Post-meeting amendments involving minor changes may be incorporated into the evaluation report, while major changes or significant new information will require reconsideration at a future meeting. If JMPS cannot reach a consensus, the proposer will be asked to provide additional data to resolve outstanding issues within a specified timeframe. The basis for recommendations to accept or reject specifications will be recorded in the evaluation. If the proposer significantly changes the manufacturing process, re-evaluation by JMPS will be required to ensure compliance with the specification. Specifications and corresponding evaluations will be published online, typically within the calendar year of the JMPS meeting at which they were considered. The publication of specifications may be delayed until supporting test methods are validated or adopted, as appropriate.
